question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{\sqrt{x}-4}{x-16} & =\frac{\sqrt{16}-4}{16-16}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{\sqrt{x}-4}{x-16} & ={lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{(\sqrt{x}-4)(\sqrt{x}+4)}{(x-16)(\sqrt{x}+4)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{{(\sqrt{x})}^{2}-{4}^{2}}{(x-16)(\sqrt{x}+4)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{x-16}{(x-16)(\sqrt{x}+4)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{16}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
